blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless heater heats water only when a tap opens. Water flows through a heat exchanger, a burner or element fires and hot water comes out as long as you need it. There's no tank to keep hot all day, so it uses less energy when you're not using water. The trade-off: it has a limit on how much hot water it can make at once, so it has to be sized for your busiest moment.

We size the unit so two showers and the dishwasher can run at once.
Minerals build up in the heat exchanger. A yearly flush keeps it running right.

items.q: Why does my tankless heater go cold in the middle of a shower?
items.preview: Often scale, a flow issue or too much demand.
items.answer: Often scale in the heat exchanger, a dirty inlet screen or more fixtures running than the unit can handle. Descaling fixes the first two.

items.q: How often should a tankless heater be descaled?
items.answer: About once a year for most homes. Homes on well water may need it more often.
Yes. We diagnose error codes, clean flame sensors and inlet screens, descale heat exchangers and replace failed parts.

items.q: Can I switch from a tank to tankless?
items.preview: Usually, with gas and venting changes.
items.answer: Usually. Most switches need a larger gas line and new venting. We check both before giving you a price.

items.q: Is tankless worth it for a family of four or five?
items.answer: Often. A properly sized unit can run two showers and the dishwasher at once. We'll look at your gas line and venting before you decide.

items.q: Can a tankless heater run on well water?
items.answer: Yes, but well water often needs softening or filtering to protect the heat exchanger.
